_meta.purpose: A PORTABLE map of the properties of laboratory tests: level (tier), biomaterial/tube, preparation, computed indices and their prerequisites. It is needed so that the draw checklist does not turn into a sheet of forty items but goes in steps: the cheap screening first, the expensive only if the screening showed something.

tiers.1: basic screening: part of the ordinary panels, cheap, available everywhere
tiers.2: clarifying: ordered on purpose, more expensive, often requires particular conditions for the draw
tiers.3: expert: expensive and/or rare, it makes sense only when there is a deviation at levels 1–2

biomaterials.serum: serum (a tube with a clot activator)

_meta.fields: tier · biomaterial · fasting · computed (calculated — not drawn) · requires (what has to be measured for the index to come out or to be readable) · note
_meta.rule: Computed indices do not go on the form as a separate item — their components are ordered instead. IMPORTANT: this rule is about THE CONTENT OF THE ORDER, not about the data. If the laboratory itself computed and printed an index (HOMA-IR, eGFR, ratios), its value is accepted, kept in labs.json and takes part in trends and thresholds on a par with the measured ones. A tier 3 test is proposed only if all of its requires have a fresh value; otherwise those are proposed first.

loinc.purpose: a compatibility layer for exchange with the outside (FHIR and the like). It does not affect the parsing of Russian lab forms: LOINC is not printed on them, matching stays by name.
loinc.source: NLM Clinical Table Search Service (clinicaltables.nlm.nih.gov, LOINC items v3) — every code was checked by a query on the code itself and reconciled with the full name
loinc.coverage: 34 codes reconciled, 13 marked as not reconciled
loinc.rule: A LOINC code is NEVER written from memory: an invented code looks like a standard and silently breaks the exchange. No confirmation — the field stays null with the status «not verified».

body_metrics._note: LOINC codes that name a BODY MEASUREMENT rather than a laboratory analyte. A measurement of the person is written where one of our metrics holds the same quantity in the same unit — `ours` names it and `unit` is the only unit accepted, because nothing here converts and a weight in pounds joining a series in kilograms is the defect this project spends its time removing. Where `ours` is null the reason says what the value is instead, so that a refusal is an answer and not a shrug.

8302-2.name: Body Height
8302-2.why: height is one field of the profile rather than a series; the bundle's value is reported so it can be set with `scholion profile --height-cm`

29463-7.name: Body Weight
29463-7.why: the same quantity our weight metric holds, in the same unit

59576-9.name: Body mass index (BMI) [Percentile] Per age and gender
59576-9.why: a percentile against an age-and-sex reference, not the index our bmi metric holds
